kryptpay: The fork has no frontend at all (program and tests only), so there is no app of its own to host.
predix: The fork's app/ is a Create React App UI with no Anchor or web3 client; it never calls the program, so hosting it would not exercise anything on devnet.
seloongmun: The fork's web/ is the create-solana-dapp counter scaffold (increment/decrement): it never calls draw, imports a ShootingIDL file that does not exist, and its build fails.
mons-dot-rehab: end_game has to be signed by the mons game server, and the client is the mons game itself; neither can be hosted as a static page.
valhalla: The app depends on server-side Next.js API routes and Clockwork/Helius services, so a static export cannot run its flow.
elyse: A static site. Its only Solana write, the token faucet, runs server-side with a sender key fetched from the author's own server; the swap page embeds Jupiter Terminal, which is mainnet-only. Nothing here can be proven on devnet without that server.
solstage-web: The app never calls its program's instructions: it uploads the filter file to Shadow Drive (mainnet-only, paid in SHDW) and then tags a PDA of program STAGYb3H… with a memo transaction. That program exists on devnet (deployed by the original author), but the flow cannot complete without a mainnet Shadow Drive upload.
stealthfolio: Swaps go through Jupiter (mainnet-only) and private trades need the Light Protocol relayer server in relayer/; there is no program of its own to deploy.
gluon-solana: Its fission/fusion instructions read a Pyth PriceUpdateV2 account no older than 60 s, and the app posts that update from Pyth Hermes; hermes.pyth.network now answers 401 without an API key, so the flow cannot run from a static page.
decentralogistics: The frontend reads and writes logistics requests through its own Express API server (api-server/, http://localhost:3000), which a static host cannot serve.
solassets-solanahackathon: The app creates its Supabase client at import time from VITE_SUPABASE_URL / VITE_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY (not in the repo), and the Tokens page reads the signed-in Supabase user before calling create_standard_token, so it cannot run without the author's Supabase project.
blocqfinance-colosseum: The Next.js app logs in and loads letters of credit through its own backend (blocq-backend, NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL); the program calls (fund, release, refund) are only reachable after that backend's auth.
tagin-solana: The frontends call local Flask/Express APIs (localhost:5000 / 5002) for products and reports.
vv-solana: The client is a MUD (Lattice) game: it boots against EVM world contracts on BSC and a gRPC indexer (VITE_WORLD_CONTRACT, VITE_GRPC_URL, ...) and Particle Network login, and it imports the program IDL from an uncommitted build artifact; the Solana program is only a side module.
gifter-escrow: Every token list and balance in the app comes from Helius DAS calls (getAssetsByOwner, getAssetBatch) to devnet.helius-rpc.com with the author's API key hard-coded in the source; we don't use someone else's key, and the public devnet RPC has no DAS methods.
autohero: The web app's story and hero flow goes through the author's backend API (VITE_API_URL via axios) before it touches the program.
tamagochi-solana-codigo: The program can never create a pet: create_tamagotchi takes tamagotchi_state as an existing Account<TamagotchiState> with no init, so the account it is meant to create must already exist and be owned by the program.
ai-saas-portal-solana: Agents and tasks are listed and added through the author's backend at ai-saas.deno.dev (fetch /agents, /tasks, /add_task, /add_agent).
zk-student: Proofs are generated server-side: the app calls a prover API (NEXT_PUBLIC_PROVER_API_URL /prove, /execute) before anything reaches the program.
solana-coloseum-hackathon: The app stores and reads its ideas through Firebase.
proof-of-anchor: The hosted part is a verifier that fetches other sites (https://<domain>/…, the GitHub API) and Noir proofs; the web app does not call the Anchor program.
zylith-solana: The shielded pool needs an off-chain ASP service and a relayer (VITE_ASP_URL, VITE_RELAYER_ADDRESS) plus wrapped-BTC/stablecoin mints the app is configured with.
demage: The app/ folder is a leftover todo template: it imports the IDL from an uncommitted target/ build and calls createProfile, which the token-2022 staking program doesn't have, so no page in it can stake, unstake or create a pool.
momimarket: The main page only wires up creating an event and listing events; joining an option is never called from it, and its 'test transaction' button sends 0 SOL to yourself. The hand-written IDL in src/lib/anchor.ts is in the pre-0.30 format with no account types and is passed to the old Program(idl, programId, provider) constructor, while the app depends on @coral-xyz/anchor 0.32.
sol-pot-turbo: The web app never calls join_game, allocate_points or claim_prize; games are started and settled by a keeper bot script (src/scripts/keeperBot.ts) that has to run somewhere on a schedule.
miner-war: Built on MagicBlock BOLT: the app needs about a dozen ECS component and system programs (programs-ecs/) deployed next to the main program, and routes play through MagicBlock's devnet router. Deferred: deploying all of them would take most of our devnet SOL budget.
toy-dfba: Auction state, orders and results are read from the author's backend (axios to localhost:3001/api/...), and the program runs through a MagicBlock ephemeral rollup.
ursusai-monorepo: The frontend reads agents and trades from its own backend and websocket (VITE_BACKEND_URL, VITE_WS_URL; ursus-backend/).
zefe-solana-breakout-submission: A Telegram Mini App that signs in and refreshes tokens through its own backend API (NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL /api/v1/token/refresh).
solsafe: Case lookups and stats come from the author's backend (REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL /api/trace, /api/stats) and evidence is fetched from IPFS.
yaycazz: The frontend's IDL (yaycazz-frontend/src/libs/idl.ts) is for a different program, "registration_program"; the fork's program has initialize / init_amm / deposite, so the app can't drive it.
solana-avatars: The app is a server-rendered Remix app: it needs its Node server, including the /api/ipfs proxy route that fetches avatar files from an IPFS gateway (local by default).
dash: The fork has only the Anchor program and its tests (the root package.json is the Anchor scaffold's lint scripts); there is no frontend to host.
fairswap: The fork has only the Anchor program and its tests (the root package.json is the Anchor scaffold's lint scripts); there is no frontend to host.
solana-program: The fork has only the Anchor program and its tests (the root package.json is the Anchor scaffold's lint scripts); there is no frontend to host.
xutasc: The fork has only the Anchor program and its tests (the root package.json is the Anchor scaffold's lint scripts); there is no frontend to host.
surge-contract: The fork has only the Anchor program and its tests (the root package.json is the Anchor scaffold's lint scripts); there is no frontend to host.
terra-ledger: The web app reads parcels, credit profiles and agent decisions from the author's backend API (/api/v1/...).
assetcli-init: It is a CLI and MCP server (src/commands, mcp-server.ts) with no web frontend.
swarmhaul: The dashboard reads from the author's API (VITE_API_URL, default api.swarmhaul.defited.com) and the repo ships agent and API services (Dockerfile.api, Dockerfile.agent).
wrapsynth: The frontend is a multi-chain (EVM/Monero) static site that talks to the fork's LP server (/api/...); it doesn't drive the Solana programs on its own.
solignition: Its core flow (request a deployment loan, repay) goes through the author's deployer service (VITE_DEPLOYER_API_URL); only deposit/withdraw would work without it.
spread-market: Settling an options epoch needs expire_market, which reads a live price oracle with at most 10 s staleness and 2% confidence (expire_market.rs L35-44, the devnet override is a TODO), so bought spreads can't be redeemed on devnet without a fresh oracle feed. Also, its faucet signs with a mint-authority secret key committed in the frontend (constants.tsx), which we won't host.
cyphercast: Its Next.js app never calls the program's real instructions: the only transaction it builds is a placeholder (app/src/lib/solana/actions.ts) with one data byte [0] and three accounts, which its own comment says mimics join_stream until the IDL encoder is added. Hosting it would show a UI that cannot complete the program's flow.
credible: Its React app's issue and verify calls are placeholders: utils/solanaUtils.js returns 'dummy-credential-id' and true without sending anything, and utils/solanaInteractions.js builds the Anchor client from an empty IDL ({}) against localhost:8899. Other screens need Okto login and a local /api backend (setupProxy to localhost:3001).
tripon: Its Next.js app was written against an older program: web/idl/anchor.json has initialize_hotel(name, verified) and a mint_membership_token with no multiplier argument and no config account, while the program at this commit needs both. As a result, both mint buttons (home and dashboard) would fail before sending. The home page also mints against mock hotels (lib/mockHotels.ts) whose owner keys nobody here controls. Making it work would mean rewriting the app's calls rather than hosting the fork's own app.
